newsitem.title: HUNGARY: State influence not good for MOL - analyst.
newsitem.headline: State influence not good for MOL - analyst.

text.p: Continued state influence would do little to change the inherent problems of Hungary's oil and gas company MOL Rt, an analyst said on Monday.
"The government's golden share gives it authority to have a veto in any structural changes," Tommy Erdei, ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett's Budapest-based analyst, told Reuters.
"MOL's top management is very good... but the middle management hasn't changed much over the last couple of years." @
Referring to last week's information that the state would probably sell another 12 to 18 percent of its stake in MOL early next year, he said the move is unlikely to bring significant improvements.
"Even if the government reduces its stake to just the golden share, it would still have a strong influence," Erdei said.
He added that according to his calculations, the imminent offering of MOL shares would be priced at around 2,400 forints, a price he considers unrealistic. @
"I don't think they would be able to sell it for 2,400," he said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares closed at 1,755 forints on Friday.
Erdei estimated that MOL's cut of the January 1 gas price increase of 18.8 percent would be between 11 to 13 percent.
"Including evironmental provisions and other costs, that would mean a more or less breakeven (result) for MOL's gas business," he said.
Last week another analyst said he expects MOL's share of the price increase to be around 15 percent. @
Erdei added that MOL's better than expected Q3 results, although encouraging, are not an indication of improving company fundamentals.
"The improved earnings of MOL were for reasons out of its control," he said, adding that taking into account the cyclical nature of the oil market he expects a turn for the worst.
"Things are going to get worse from here on," he said.
On Friday, ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett's company update on MOL said "we advise shareholders to sell into strength" and said it maintained a long-term negative outlook on MOL.
